title: Action de Galois sur Teichmüller : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is the start (sheet '1') of a fresh write-up inside the Teichmüller/Galois notes. It sets up the canonical geometry of the basic building block, the conformal sphere with three marked points (the pair of pants M_{0,3}). Its purpose is to fix sign and orientation conventions before gluing such blocks.

The set-up is a conformal 2-sphere Σ (≅ P^1(C)) with a 3-element subset J = {R_i}.
- The holomorphic automorphisms preserving J form exactly S_J ≅ S_3 (the Möbius transformations permuting 0, 1, ∞).
- The full group of conformal and anticonformal automorphisms of (Σ, J) is Γ ≅ S_J × {1, τ}.
- τ is the unique antiholomorphic involution fixing each R_i: complex conjugation in the model {0, 1, ∞}. It commutes with S_J.
- The NB notes that the antipodal map is not in Γ, because it does not stabilise J.

Canonical metric. In the conformal class, the round (constant-curvature) metrics form PSL_2(C)/SO(3) ≅ H^3. The finite group S_3 has a unique fixed point there: C_3 fixes a geodesic, and the involutions cut it to one point. Hence there is a unique S_J-invariant round metric up to a scalar λ > 0. This identifies Σ canonically with the unit sphere of a 3-dimensional Euclidean space E_J.

Since τ commutes with S_J, it is an isometry of this metric, namely the orthogonal reflection in a plane V. So Σ_R = Σ ∩ V is a great circle containing J, and V = R-span of the R_j is 2-dimensional.

The three Z/2-torsors (3):
- ϖ = orientations of Σ (equivalently of E);
- ω = orientations of J (cyclic orders), equivalently orientations of the real circle Σ_R;
- ε = π_0(Σ − Σ_R), the two hemispheres, = π_0(E − V) = π_0((E/V) − 0), i.e. the orientations of the line E/V.

(3 bis) states ω ∧ ε ∧ ϖ = 1, so any one torsor is the product of the other two. Grothendieck calls this 'Stokes': an orientation of the sphere plus a choice of hemisphere gives the boundary orientation of the equator. Equivalently, or(E) = or(V) ⊗ or(E/V).

Next page. The R_j form an equilateral triangle, Σ R_j = 0, and V ≅ Ker(R^J → R) with the S_J-invariant form q(R_j) = 1, i.e. x² − xy + y². The polar axis is Δ = V^⊥ ≅ R(ε). Hence E ≅ V_J(R) ⊕ R(ε), with S_J acting tautologically on V_J and by the sign character on Δ. This sign action is correct: a transposition, e.g. z ↦ 1/z, exchanges the upper and lower half-planes.

The left margin says:
- the category of (Σ, J) is equivalent to a category of linear-algebra data, roughly (Euclidean 3-space, 3-point set in a plane);
- one could write V(J, ϖ), E(J, ϖ);
- warning: do not confuse this situation with the 'cubes' / elementary situations {x, y, z}, {α, β, γ} elsewhere in the notes.

The aim is evidently a functorial, sign-precise description of the M_{0,3} building block: its real structure, hemispheres (the two triangles of the canonical cell decomposition / trivial dessin) and orientation torsors. This is preparatory to assembling the Teichmüller 'Lego' and tracking orientations under gluing.
errors: No mathematical errors found. Every claim checks: Γ ≅ S_3 × Z/2; uniqueness of the S_3-invariant round metric up to scale; τ is an isometric reflection, so V is 2-dimensional; the torsor identity holds; the sign action on Δ is right.
Minor imprecision: 'métrique homogène' should be read as constant-curvature (round) metric in the conformal class; homogeneity alone is not what singles it out, S_J-invariance is.

The name 'Stokes' for (3 bis) is a heuristic (boundary-orientation convention). The precise sign of the identification ω ≅ ε ∧ ϖ depends on an outward- or inward-normal convention not fixed on this page.

ideas.what: Automorphism group of (P^1, 3 points) including antiholomorphic maps is S_3 × {1, τ}, with τ the canonical real structure fixing the three points
ideas.modern_name: canonical real structure on M_{0,3} / pair of pants; anharmonic group
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses canonical structures on the (0,3) building blocks and the cartographic/real picture; exact statement unsure

ideas.what: Unique S_3-invariant round metric, identifying Σ with the unit sphere in a Euclidean 3-space E_J ≅ V_J(R) ⊕ sign, three points forming an equilateral triangle on the equator
ideas.modern_name: decomposition of the S_3 representation as standard ⊕ sign; barycenter of a finite group in H^3

ideas.what: Three Z/2-torsors (orientation of sphere ϖ, cyclic order of J ω, hemispheres ε) with product relation ω ∧ ε ∧ ϖ = 1, called a 'Stokes formula'
ideas.modern_name: multiplicativity of orientation torsors in short exact sequences / boundary orientation convention
ideas.where_published: orientation-torsor bookkeeping of this kind is used in SGA-style texts, but not this specific statement

ideas.what: Equivalence of the category of conformal spheres with 3 marked points to a category of Euclidean linear-algebra data (E, V, J)
ideas.modern_name: rigidification of M_{0,3} as a groupoid

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up a fully functorial, sign-precise linear-algebra model of the (0,3) building block, including the hemisphere torsor ε and its S_3 sign action. The evident purpose is to control orientation and sign conventions when gluing pants in the Teichmüller tower. This kind of explicit orientation-torsor bookkeeping for the 'Lego' is not spelled out in the published Lego literature (Hatcher–Thurston, Moore–Seiberg, Bakalov–Kirillov, Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps). It is, however, mathematically routine.
missed.quote: On a ω ∧ ε ∧ ϖ = 1 i.e. ω ≃ ε∧ϖ, ε ≃ ω∧ϖ, ϖ ≃ ω∧ε ; c'est la formule de Stokes
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Marginal. It could serve as a clean convention for signs and orientations in GT-actions on pants decompositions, but specialists would regard it as standard.

deep.surprise_reason: A careful, routine set-up of the canonical geometry of P^1 minus three points (real structure, round metric, orientation torsors). Correct and elegantly functorial, but contains nothing a specialist would find new.
transcription_corrections: Margin top: likely 'Attention à ne pas confondre la situation [présente], qui est..., avec celles des « cubes » ou situations élémentaires {x,y,z}, {α,β,γ}... (1)'. The machine reading 'confondre ... à celle des' is garbled.
'τ est l'unique antiautomorphisme ≠ 1': the '+1' in the image is '≠ 1', and 'anti' is written above 'automorphisme'. Mathematically τ must be antiholomorphic.

Margin middle: 'dans la catégorie des (Σ, J), équivalente (2) à celle des couples (E, J?) ...'. The objects named after 'couples' are illegible. The reading 'ϖ, β' and 'J plan dans (Σ_n)' is unreliable; probably E a Euclidean 3-space and J a 3-point set on the unit sphere spanning a plane.
In (3), the first line's comment reads 'ens. des deux orientations de Σ, ou de E', consistent with ϖ = Ω(Σ) ≃ Ω(E_J).
'V le R-sous-espace vectoriel de E engendré par les R_J' should read 'engendré par les R_j' (indices in J).
